title: i18n-kit translation catalog
description: Translations for one locale and one namespace. Written by the tool and by humans. A failed translation is recorded with no message field at all, never with source-language text standing in.

message.description: The translated ICU text. ABSENT when the last attempt failed. Absence is the honest state; source-language text here would make a missing-key check pass while hiding the failure.

origin.description: Who wrote the current text. Set to 'human' automatically when the text stops matching contentHash, which is how a hand edit is detected without anyone remembering to set a flag.

review.description: 'approved' is stricter than a human origin: exempt even from context-change churn. Intended for signed-off copy.

sourceHash.description: Over the NORMALIZED source message plus its argument contract. A mismatch means this translation may be wrong.

contextHash.description: Over the NORMALIZED comment, context, class, placeholder descriptions and examples, and maxLength. A mismatch means this translation may be lower quality, which is never a reason to fail a build.

contentHash.description: Over the EXACT bytes of the translated message. Deliberately not normalized: a human's typographic correction is precisely the edit normalization would erase, and detecting it is the whole point.

reason.description: The validation rule that rejected the response, and the detail.

kind.description: Raised by the model during translation. A cultural reference that does not travel is exactly the problem no static check can find.

qa.description: Results of an `i18n qa` review. Advisory only: findings are never applied automatically, because doing so would overwrite text including human text.

suggestion.description: Proposed replacement text. Applying it is a separate, explicit human action.

at.description: A date, not a timestamp, and restamped only when the message actually changes. Keeps an audit trail without churning diffs on every run.

provenance.description: Model and prompt version are recorded but deliberately NOT hashed. Hashing them would make one prompt tweak silently rebill the entire catalog. Regenerating after a model change is an explicit command.
